title: Río de la Plata
capsule: The Provincias Unidas del Río de la Plata declared independence from Spain on 9 July 1816 and governed a loosely confederated set of provinces in the Viceroyalty's former territory, but the entity was never fully territorially consolidated — Paraguay became independent in 1811, the Banda Oriental (Uruguay) was contested with Portugal/Brazil, and Upper Peru followed its own path. The Buenos Aires-dominated central government collapsed amid interprovincial federalist-unitarian conflict during the 1820s, producing a period of disintegration. The Argentine Confederation, formally constituted in 1831 after the Pact of the Federal League, succeeded it, with the entity in the dataset spanning the transitional years of contested sovereignty that preceded the 1853 constitution.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is poorly attested for this period; the Río de la Plata entity had no fixed border with Bolivia, Paraguay, or the Banda Oriental, and provincial authority was contested.
